summary: Self-hosted mode now pings Redis before every request; if Redis can't be reached, every page redirects to a new public /redis-configuration-error help page (which redirects home once Redis works). Also adds Redis to CI, removes unused early_access action, and whitespace cleanup in many views.

statements.why: No login/data/money/secret problem: the only new open page (/redis-configuration-error) is a static help page. Behaviour risks (self-hosted lock-out, per-request Redis ping) are worth knowing but are not security/data-loss issues; see misses.

statements.text: + New server code that lists data. /redis-configuration-error
statements.why: It lists no data: PagesController#redis_configuration_error just renders a static 'Redis Configuration Required' help page (blank layout), reachable without login (skip_authentication) and only meaningful on self-hosted installs.

statements.text: The agent changed the accountable sparkline, accounts, ... vehicle parts of your server in ways plain can't describe yet. Ask the agent what they do differently.
statements.why: None of those features were edited. One check was added to SelfHostable (prepend_before_action :verify_self_host_config) that, on self-hosted installs only, sends every page to /redis-configuration-error when Redis can't be reached. The card lists ~180 'changed' areas without ever saying that.
New minimal layout used by the error page.
CI now runs a Redis service and sets REDIS_URL.

misses.what: Self-hosted installs without a reachable Redis are now completely blocked: every page (including login) redirects to the Redis setup page instead of loading.

Every request on self-hosted installs opens a new Redis connection (Redis.new.ping, never closed) and only CannotConnectError is caught; a Redis timeout or auth error would make every page error out instead of showing the help page.
